Ashburnham Community School
Welcome
A warm welcome from the Head of School,
Jonathan East
Located in Chelsea, West London, Ashburnham is a happy, friendly school where children achieve academic excellence. I am immensely proud to be the Head of School, working with a talented and committed team of leaders, teachers and support staff. We are one of four schools in the Fox Federation. The other schools are Fox Primary, Avondale Primary, Avonmore Primary, Park Walk and St Anne’s nursery. Ofsted has praised all the school’s curriculum, robust safeguarding procedures, behaviour, teaching and learning and commented on the strong sense of community in each school.
The Fox Federation is unique in that it ensures each school retains its individual identity but at the same time has unique benefits of working together to make each stronger than if on its own.
Benefits of Fox Federation:
Ashburnham is a one form entry school, with up to thirty children in each year group. We have an on-site nursery for 3 and 4 year olds. Our Nursery is located in our main school building so the children benefit from joining in with older children including at lunch time eating and playing with the reception children and doing PE in the main playground and hall. Both our reception and nursery children have the opportunity to learn in their indoor and outdoor classrooms which have to be seen to be believed. Please click to see our ‘admissions’ page which has more information on our Nursery and Reception classes – the most common admission year groups.
We offer a modern, spacious, well-resourced learning environment for all children which supports children’s development. When walking around the school, visitors always comment on how purposeful, calm and nurturing the atmosphere is. We are also lucky enough to have the largest playground in the borough, fully equipped with a huge climbing frame, a tree house, a reading shed and two sports pitches, so there is plenty of space for children to play and socialise during break times.
Our school embodies strong values which underpin all we do. Five of these values: curiosity, collaboration, kindness, inclusion and respect are shared across the federation and the sixth is chosen each year as a result of a whole school vote organised by our pupil council.
We have high expectations of all our children, both academically and socially and aim for all children to meet these expectations through our engaging, exciting curriculum, which is complimented by a rich program of enriching experiences, community events, trips, workshops and clubs. We are passionate about ensuring that all children leave Ashburnham as well-rounded, confident and articulate young people, having achieved excellent results and who are fully prepared to succeed in their next stage of education.
We are proud of the diverse community that we serve and as a school welcome any opportunity to work with our parents and carers to provide the best opportunities for all of our children. We work with a number of external organisations, including All Child, which allows us to meet the needs of all of our pupils and work towards developing a lifelong love of learning so they can achieve their absolute potential.
I hold school tours throughout the year and I would very much welcome the opportunity to meet you and show you around our lovely school in person.
Please feel free to have a look at our school instagram account to gain more of an insight into life at Ashburnham.
Ashburnham Community School17 Blantyre StreetLondon SW10 0DT
Tel.: +44 (0) 207 352 5740 Fax: +44 (0) 207 351 7669

Ashburnham Community School
Curriculum
Our curriculum intent and approach to implementation sit alongside our Federation Mission, Vision and Values. The links below will redirect you to the Fox Federation website.
Fox Federation Curriculum Intent:
Our curriculum is ambitious, broad and balanced. We meet and exceed the expectations of the National Curriculum. Our curriculum is knowledge rich, ensuring children build key vocabulary and concepts at every stage. We plan the curriculum carefully, with a clear progression of knowledge and skills from the EYFS and to KS2, leading to greater disciplinary knowledge and skills over time, preparing children for transition to Secondary Schools. Our curriculum develops aspiration and appreciation and awareness of the wider world and children’s position within it, with a strong focus on representation, developing strong oracy skills and critical thinking. We develop cultural capital across the curriculum, through planned enrichment linked specifically to the curriculum and through celebration of diverse contributions to fields of learning and achievement. British Values are woven across the curriculum. In this way we make a difference through understanding and living our values.
Fox Federation Curriculum Implementation:
HIgh quality CPD and a commitment to learning from research and best practice lies at the heart of our curriculum implementation. Staff at every level are provided with extensive opportunities to develop their own subject knowledge and pedagogy to ensure the curriculum can be delivered effectively with maximum impact. Subject and senior leaders support all staff to develop their expertise through routine co-planning, modelling of lessons, as well as coaching and monitoring. Subject specialists are used to teach key areas of the curriculum, to sustain the highest levels of expertise, including: PE, Music, Art and Mindfulness. Vocabulary is taught explicitly and effectively across the whole curriculum. There is a high level of talk in all lessons, applying key vocabulary and allowing for reasoning and depth of discussion in learning. Learning is made accessible to all, by clear coverage of prior knowledge and learning, and, within each lesson, consistent scaffolding, chunking of new learning, opportunities for talk and feedback. Pupils with specific additional needs work against their termly target trackers, and only in some cases resulting in alternative learning tasks being designed. Opportunities for depth are provided through questioning, reasoning, depth tasks and reading beyond the curriculum. Homework is focused in the areas that have the greatest impact on pupil progress: Maths Fluency, Reading, Spelling and Handwriting. Formative assessment is used routinely within lessons, in order to address pupil misconceptions. Summative assessments are used termly to track how pupils are progressing against the curriculum. All lessons allow pupils to practise our core values of Respect, Resilience, Collaboration, Curiosity and Inclusion.
If you want more information about our curriculum, please contact our head of curriculum and standards, Emma Madden Info@foxprimary.co.uk

Ashburnham Community School
PE
Children are asked to wear their PE kit to school each day that they have their PE or dance lessons. PE kit should be plain navy blue with no logos visible and should be appropriate for the season. Families can purchase PE kit from any store of their choice but the following links that contain affordable options may help this process.
Navy blue tracksuit: top and bottoms
Navy blue shorts: breathable or cotton
Navy blue t-shirt: breathable or cotton
Trainers: any appropriate trainer – these can be any colour as long as they are appropriate. No studs or boots are allowed.
Physical Education is of paramount importance at Ashburnham. We have a full-time specialist PE teacher who teaches all the pupils in the school, and our aim is to ensure health, wellbeing and participation at all ages and stages, from Nursery to Y6. We have experienced huge success in competitive sports and in the proportion of pupils partaking in a huge range of activities, building in them health, confidence and love of sport.

Ashburnham Community School
Pupil Premium
Ashburnham Community School is committed to supporting all children to ensure they make expected or better than expected progress. In particular, the school is required to “identify and support pupils who have significant disadvantages so that their progress is maximised” (Ofsted). We strongly believe that all children can and do succeed at Ashburnham, regardless of any obstacle that could prevent such progress. This is partly due to the fact that the school effectively spends Pupil Premium (PP) funding.
We are required to demonstrate and justify how the Pupil Premium money that the school gets is spent wisely. This document will outline how Pupil Premium funding is allocated.
The school aims to strategically spend the Pupil Premium funding in order to close any gaps in attainment. A significant amount of funding is spent on direct academic support to ensure that all children fulfil their potential and make excellent progress in reading, writing and maths by the end of Year Six. In addition, a substantial amount of money is spent on social, emotional and mental health priorities across the school, with the aim of ensuring all children are able to access the curriculum effectively. We aim to ensure all children are able to achieve their best, regardless of personal circumstance.
Pupil Premium Strategy
Narrowing the Gap at Ashburnham: an explanation of how disadvantaged children achieved compared to other children
At Ashburnham, the expectation is that all pupils in the school (excepting those with special educational needs who are unable to access the curriculum) will reach at least at least age related expectations by the end of Year 6 and make excellent progress.
The school receives extra funding to support children who come from low income families (disadvantaged pupils – DP). The school is effective at ensuring equality of outcomes for all pupils. We are determined to ensure this continues with successive cohorts of children and we endeavour to achieve this through careful analysis of data, targeted interventions and above all consistent, high-quality teaching.
